title: Properness of flat separated families with connected proper fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $h:Y\to S$ be a separated flat morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume that for every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the fibre $Y_{\bar s}$ is nonempty, connected and proper over $\Omega$. Then $h$ is proper. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts, and finite presentation additionally requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed, with universal closedness tested after every base change. Locally Noetherian has the meaning of [pqf-def-locnoeth]; the chartwise and topological morphism-property conventions are [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

source.place: Section 1.1, final paragraph, printed pp.131--132 (flat separated finite-presentation spaces with connected proper geometric fibres), invoking EGA III-1 Section 5.5. Local Deligne PDF WANTED; primary Numdam PDF read online. For schemes the criterion is EGA IV-3 (literature/ega/EGA-IV-3_PMIHES-28-1966.pdf), Corollaire 15.7.10 with Proposition 15.7.9, printed pp.245--247: separated of finite type, universally submersive (here: flat, finitely presented and surjective, hence universally open and surjective), geometrically connected fibres, proper fibre at y implies proper at y.

proof.text: By the strict-local properness test it suffices to prove properness after base change along each $T=S_{(\bar s)}\to S$. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $q:X=Y\times_ST\to T$. The strict-henselization functoriality statement says that $A$ is strictly henselian local and identifies its closed point. Base-change permanence makes $q$ flat and of finite presentation, and separatedness persists: its diagonal is a base change of the original closed-immersion diagonal. Every geometric point of $T$, composed with $T\to S$, is a geometric point of $S$; associativity of sheaf fibre products identifies its fibre with the original geometric fibre. Thus all geometric fibres of $q$ are nonempty, connected and proper.

source.place: Tag 08K1 and strict-local test; flat and finite-presentation base change: Tags 03MO, 03XR; strict local ring: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX.

proof.text: Let $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, and choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$. Its spectrum is an fpqc cover of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by the field-extension-cover lemma. The base change of $X_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to this cover is a geometric fibre of $q$, hence proper by Step 1. Fpqc descent of properness therefore gives that the entire closed fibre $X_k$ is proper over $k$. It is nonempty, since its geometric base change is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0422, properness descent along a field extension; field spectra: topologies.tex fpqc covering.

proof.text: The pair $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ is henselian because $A$ is strictly henselian. The map $q$ is separated and of finite type, since finite presentation implies finite type. Apply henselian proper-clopen lifting with $I=\mathfrak m_A$ and $Z=X_k$, the whole closed fibre (which is open and closed in itself). It gives an open and closed $W\subseteq X$, proper over $T$, whose closed fibre is all of $X_k$. All hypotheses are now available; properness of $X$ has not been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CWI, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, applied to the entire proper closed fibre.

proof.text: The flat locally finitely presented map $q$ is open. Since $W$ is open in $X$, its image $q(W)$ is open in $T$ and contains the closed point by nonemptiness of $X_k$. Every open subset of the spectrum of a local ring containing the closed point is the entire spectrum: it contains a principal open $D(a)$ around that point, where $a\notin\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit. Consequently $W$ meets every fibre of $q$. Fix any geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$. A point of $W$ over its image and the representative of $\bar t$ have a common field extension; the fibre-product universal property gives a point of $W_{\bar t}$. This is the field-point meaning of surjectivity, so $W_{\bar t}$ is nonempty. It is clopen in connected $X_{\bar t}$, hence equals $X_{\bar t}$.

source.place: Tag 042S; elementary local-spectrum and connected-clopen argument, using field-valued point classes.

proof.text: If $X\setminus W$ had a point, choose a field-valued representative of it and extend that field to an algebraic closure. Its composite with $q$ is a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, and the representative defines a point of $X_{\bar t}\setminus W_{\bar t}$, contrary to Step 4. Thus the open subspace $W$ has all points of $X$ and equals $X$, including its restricted structure sheaf. Since $W\to T$ is proper, $q$ is proper. This holds for every $S_{(\bar s)}$, so the strict-local test gives properness of $h$. If $S$ is empty the same test has no geometric points and gives the assertion directly.

split_report.summary: Expanded fibrewise properness through the algebraic-space henselian proper-clopen lifting lemma. Properness of the closed fibre is descended from a geometric fibre using fpqc descent; flatness makes the lifted part meet every fibre, and geometric connectedness removes the complement. Three smaller statement-only inputs, no clause relabelling, no Lean attachment or Mathlib leaf. Preserved hypotheses and conclusion, adding only explicit existing definition references.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NQ-2077aa5bb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all three new nodes in full against Stacks 0CWI (spaces-more-morphisms lines 8483-8496), 0422 with 03YH (spaces-descent lines 1666 and 992), 08K1 with 084W (spaces-limits) and 083R. The five steps are correct. Step 1: the strict-local test applies because h is finitely presented; clause (1) of the strict-henselization functoriality node gives a strictly henselian local ring; flatness and finite presentation pass to the base change; the separated diagonal is a base change; geometric fibres are identified by associativity of fibre products. Step 2: Spec Omega -> Spec k is an fpqc cover, the scheme-target/space-source fpqc node gives that the closed fibre X_k is proper, and X_k is nonempty. Step 3: 0CWI with I=m_A and Z=X_k; every hypothesis holds. Step 4: q is an open map, an open subset of Spec A containing the closed point is everything, a common field extension gives a point of W over each geometric point, and the clopen W_tbar fills the connected fibre. Step 5: there are no points outside W, so W=X and the strict-local test gives h proper. Properness of X is never assumed. Local Noetherianity of S is never used; that is a harmless surplus hypothesis, and the parent's use (Picard step 4) is matched. New nodes: the clopen-lift node matches 0CWI exactly (edge cases Z empty, I=0) and is not the scheme node lem-per (0CT9). The fpqc node is not a duplicate: the existing nodes are scheme-only and the fppf locality node does not cover Omega/k. The strict-local test is a true agent corollary (08K1 = lem-sfb-space-eventually-proper on an affine etale neighbourhood, then 083R or fppf descent over a surjective etale family; the converse is base change), is more than a few lines, and restates no clause of the item. DAG searches (0CWI, 0CT9, 0422, 08K1, 083R, 15.7.10, fpqc+proper, connected+clopen) found no duplicate. Batch-5 flags: def-trf-algebraic-space, the jointly-surjective-family definition, trf fibre products, sfb morphism-property definitions, fppf locality and universal openness are all general definitions or generic tools. None is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so they are not a RETURN reason. lean.note: The helper is the canonical Yoneda map of the specified field-valued point. The fibre is the existing enlargedFibreProduct, owned together with enlargedFibreProductFst by def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product; ConnectedSpace on its existing Point topology includes nonemptiness. Finite presentation is quasi-compactness, quasi-compact diagonal and MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation. The theorem node for the enlarged ringed site is not used as an owner of these plain definitions. No source statement or Lean source changed.
